name: Undervolt your Radeon — cooler and quieter, usually for free
goal: Lower temps and fan noise — often with the same or slightly better performance, because a cooler card holds its boost longer. An undervolt that goes too far just gets unstable and resets; you nudge it back and you're fine. It's the safest knob on the card.
tool: You'll use AMD's own tool — Adrenalin — nothing to install.
steps: Right-click the desktop → AMD Software: Adrenalin Edition.
Performance → Tuning → Custom; turn on GPU Tuning, set voltage to Manual.
Lower max voltage (mV) by a small step — 25 to 50 mV to start. Apply.
Play a demanding game or loop a benchmark for 20 to 30 minutes.
Stable? Drop another 25 to 50 mV and retest. Crash, artifacts, or a black screen? Step back up one increment — that's your limit.
range: Many recent Radeons settle around 50 to 120 mV under stock — but this is the silicon lottery; your chip's stable point is its own. Find it by stepping, don't paste a number from a video.
discretion: Advisory. You're making the change in AMD's tool, at your discretion — an undervolt won't hurt the hardware, but confirming stability is on you, and you should check your card's warranty terms. Compy never touches your voltage — it just measures whether it worked.
